import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_88/test_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_88/test_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_88/test_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_88/test_3.csv"
]

# Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source_files[0], index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source_files[1], index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv(source_files[2], index_col=0)
df3 = pd.read_csv(source_files[3], index_col=0)

# The target schema is only ['TrackID'] (integer).
# All source tables share the same schema, but target only requires TrackID.
# According to hints:
# - Since all source tables have the same schema, UNION is preferred.
# - We must use all source tables.
# - We only need the TrackID column.
# - We should combine all TrackID values from all sources.
# - Remove duplicates to match target examples style (unique TrackID values).
# - TrackID is integer in sources and target.

# Extract TrackID column from each source
trackid_0 = df0[['TrackID']]
trackid_1 = df1[['TrackID']]
trackid_2 = df2[['TrackID']]
trackid_3 = df3[['TrackID']]

# Concatenate all TrackID columns (union)
all_trackids = pd.concat([trackid_0, trackid_1, trackid_2, trackid_3], ignore_index=True)

# Drop duplicates to get unique TrackID values
unique_trackids = all_trackids.drop_duplicates().reset_index(drop=True)

# Ensure TrackID is integer type (as per target schema)
unique_trackids['TrackID'] = unique_trackids['TrackID'].astype(int)

# Save the result to the target path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_88/target_multisource_cot.csv"
unique_trackids.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
